area: Planning source seal refreshes its digest and timestamp on amendment but never advances amendmentEpoch
finding: A governed re-import of an amended task card updates the seal's contentDigest and sealedAt while leaving amendmentEpoch at its initial value. The field is therefore inert: it cannot distinguish a first sealing from an amended one, cannot order two amendments, and cannot tell a consumer how many times a contract has been revised. A digest proves only difference. It answers whether the bytes changed, not whether the change was a governed amendment, nor which of two observed seals is later. Any consumer that needs generation ordering — drift detection comparing a cached seal against the current one, a reviewer deciding whether acceptance criteria moved since a claim was taken, a downstream repository mirroring planning state — has no monotonic signal to read, and the one field designed to carry it silently reports zero.
expectedBehavior: The epoch must advance exactly when the sealed contract changes, and the seal write must be the only place that decides it, so no caller can produce a seal whose digest moved while its epoch stood still. A seal whose digest differs from its recorded predecessor while its epoch is unchanged is an internally inconsistent record and should be rejected rather than written. Whichever surface performs the amendment — a forced re-import, an explicit reseal, or a future amendment command — must go through that single writer.
evidenceOrRepro: 2026-08-16, ATM-GOV-0369 amendment 1. The planning card was amended to rewrite ACC-2 and add ACC-5 and ACC-6, then re-imported through the governed protected surface. The ledger seal moved from contentDigest sha256:5bb87c21a98310a3... sealedAt 2026-08-13T23:57:01.707Z to contentDigest sha256:3fb8c689af7fc595b1ba31f14b7f6f4029d9e4c6a3b4bb5ce51a292c7dc3c540 sealedAt 2026-08-15T16:17:58.338Z, while amendmentEpoch remained 0 in both. A following `tasks seal-plan-source --dry-run` reported skip-no-change, confirming the import had already written the seal it intended to write; the epoch was not omitted by a missing second step but simply never advanced. The amendment itself was substantive: acceptance count rose from four to six and requiredTestCaseIds from four to six.
followUp: Make the epoch a property of the seal writer rather than of any caller, and add coverage for the case this instance exposes: same task, two successive amendments, where the second seal must be provably later than the first without comparing timestamps. Worth recording as the general rule — a versioning field that some write paths maintain and others ignore is worse than no field, because consumers trust it. Related to [ATM-BUG-2026-08-16-001], filed from the same session's planning-source work.
